clinician.final_diagnosis: Gastric outlet obstruction due to duodenal wall circumferential thickening with adjacent inflammatory stranding from transitional cell carcinoma metastasis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old male with history of stage IV transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) treated with neo-adjuvant chemotherapy, radiation, radical cystectomy with ileal conduit, and sigmoid colostomy presented with a 5-week history of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. CT imaging on admission (E001) revealed circumferential thickening and inflammatory stranding at the descending/transverse duodenal junction with adjacent inflammatory stranding, plus diffuse biliary and pancreatic duct dilatation (double duct sign). Upper endoscopy (E003) confirmed duodenal stenosis with significant edema and congestion, traversable only with an ultrathin endoscope; initial biopsies were nondiagnostic. Colonoscopy (E004) identified a mass at the hepatic flexure with biopsy-confirmed invasive transitional cell carcinoma, establishing the diagnosis of metastatic TCC. The patient underwent placement of a Wall Flex metal stent (22 mm × 120 mm) to alleviate the gastric outlet obstruction (E005). Chemotherapy was planned by oncology, but the patient progressively deteriorated and expired one month later after establishing comfort care only.
